tools.name: search
tools.description: Find passages of legislation and court decisions. Answers with the passages themselves (an article, a paragraph of a judgment), each with its document, date, id and url. A query that names a text ("art. 6:162 BW", "§ 823 BGB", "ECLI:NL:HR:2019:2006", "32016R0679 art 17") is answered with that text f

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Read a document or one part of it in its official wording: a whole short text, one article (element), everything under a chapter, or the text as it stood on a date. One article of a law comes with the leading decisions on it: those cited most by the decisions that cite the article. Long documents co

tools.name: get_outline
tools.description: The structure of a document: its parts, chapters and articles with their headings and element ids. Use it to find the right article of a long law before reading it.

tools.name: get_citations
tools.description: What cites a document or one of its articles (direction "in": the leading ones first, those the other citing documents cite most, each with the passage that cites it), or what it cites (direction "out"), with the places where. Targets we do not hold are listed as written. To search inside the citing

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: The sources that are loaded, per jurisdiction: what each one holds, its languages, how many documents and as of which day. With a jurisdiction: also its institutions (courts, legislators), what is held of each and what is not.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_document" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.
